body.statement:
The response-boundary theorem shows that \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}primitive\text{-}clt}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}multiplier\text{-}law}\) alone do not imply coverage, even over a singleton experiment class satisfying the proposed margin-rate window.  First determine a minimal, faithfully stated, independently checkable uniform response condition that excludes the collapsing-variance construction without assuming the desired critical-value or coverage conclusion.  Candidate ingredients include response-interiority, nondegeneracy of endpoint-relevant variances, relative consistency of the multiplier variance, or quantitative anti-concentration.  Then, over the subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) satisfying the selected condition, determine whether
\[
n\kappa_n^3\to\infty,
\qquad
(n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n),
\qquad
t_n=o(\kappa_n)
\]
imply
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P}
\Pr_{\mathbb P}\!\left\{
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)
\right\}\geq1-\alpha,
\]
where the infimum is over that repaired subclass.  The additional condition must be stated in primitive response-law or multiplier-law terms and must not encode coverage itself.  This question concerns sufficiency only; whether \(n\kappa_n^3\) is sharp for rare-margin optimal-face switching remains a separate question after the response-boundary prerequisite is settled.
body.justification: The open sufficiency question is retained only on a response-regular subclass that excludes the proved singleton counterexample by primitive, independently checkable conditions.
body.gap: A minimal noncircular response-interiority, nondegenerate-variance, relative variance-consistency, or anti-concentration condition has not yet been fixed, and uniform face localization and quantile validity under the proposed margin-rate window remain unproved after that repair.
body.consumer: A positive answer would provide a usable simultaneous selector-envelope tuning regime together with explicit response-support or variance diagnostics required for its application.

obligation.what_is_open: Identify a minimal noncircular uniform response-law or resampling condition that excludes response-boundary degeneration, then determine whether the proposed margin and numerical-step rates imply simultaneous endpoint coverage on that repaired class.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximations are absolute metrics and remain valid when all endpoint-relevant variances collapse. They therefore provide neither relative variance consistency nor anti-concentration at the critical quantile, and the singleton construction gives actual undercoverage under every deterministic schedule.
obligation.attempted: The direct route from uniform bounded-Lipschitz approximation through the joint directional derivative and numerical delta map was stress-tested on the vanishing Bernoulli response array. Both approximation errors vanish, but the all-zero event has a nonvanishing probability and forces a zero multiplier critical value, so the route fails before rare-margin face localization becomes relevant.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved response-boundary theorem constructs one fixed \(2\times2\) experiment \(\mathbb P^0\) such that both bounded-Lipschitz approximation discrepancies converge to zero, but for every deterministic schedule \(t\),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\!\left\{[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\}
\leq1-e^{-\lambda}<1-\alpha.
\]
The remaining problem is therefore not derivable from the frozen approximation assumptions: it first requires a noncircular uniform response-interiority, nondegenerate-variance, relative variance-consistency, or anti-concentration condition, followed by a new uniform face-localization and quantile argument under the displayed \(\kappa_n\) and \(t_n\) rates.
